what: serving speed of the API (backlog item 13); not accuracy
caveat: the CI test bundle has untrained weights: these numbers measure serving speed only, never accuracy
where: Claude Code cloud session container (shared VM), 2026-11-09
server: scripts/bench_app.py: app/api/main.py's create_app, one uvicorn worker, rate limiter opened wide
image: one synthetic 448x448 JPEG, sent repeatedly; 10 warm-up requests not counted
differs_from_the_api_image: this run used torch 2.15.0+cu132 (a CUDA build from PyPI, run on CPU), not the image's torch 2.14.0 CPU build, and no Docker container; memory in particular may differ from the image (CUDA libraries load even when unused). The dispatch-only workflow .github/workflows/benchmark.yml measures on a GitHub runner with the CPU build.
reading: throughput stays at about 43 to 54 images a second from 1 to 20 users while median latency grows from 16.8 ms to 458.8 ms: one uvicorn worker running the test bundle's single network on 4 CPUs is CPU-bound, so concurrent requests queue. More workers or a lighter model would be the levers; not measured here.
not_the_champion: the champion bundle runs three networks per image (the 3-seed ensemble); its per-image compute is larger, so its latency and throughput are not these numbers. Measuring it needs the champion bundle (a release asset the owner uploads, as for item 6).
